title: 2 on 2 Continuous Transition
description: A continuous full-ice 2-on-2 transition drill that connects line-rush offense, defensive gap control, breakouts, and immediate counterattacks using one live puck.
coaching_points: Defensemen play a tight gap and communicate with their partner.
Forwards support each other and keep sticks available as outlets.
Create 2-on-1 situations after entering the offensive zone.
Transition immediately when the puck is saved, cleared, or broken out.

title: Strip Transitions V1 & V2
description: A two-part strip-and-transition progression where players lift or knock a puck free along the wall, transition immediately, and find a teammate timing a route into shooting space.
coaching_points: Angle the puck carrier along the boards before attacking the stick or puck.
Recover the puck and get the head up immediately.
The support player times the jump into open ice and presents a target.
Progress from stick lift strips to board-assisted puck separation.

title: Run Ragged Small Area Game
description: A small-area passing game where three forwards move around a four-cone box while a defender pressures the puck. After every pass, the passer moves to the open cone; after a set number of passes the offense can shoot.
coaching_points: Pass and immediately move to the open cone.
Players away from the puck stay available and communicate.
Defender uses stops, starts, and an active stick to disrupt passing lanes.
Add a second defender or shrink the area as players improve.

title: Back to Back Small Area Game
description: A compact game with two nets placed back-to-back in the middle of the playing area. Teams compete freely for possession and can attack the opposing net from any side.
coaching_points: Use the net as a screen and protection tool.
Change direction quickly when the direct route is closed.
Players without the puck create support on both sides of the nets.
Keep shifts short and competitive.

title: Offense then Backcheck to DZC
description: A continuous 5-on-5 sequence where a group attacks in-zone, then on the whistle backchecks the length of the ice and organizes into defensive-zone coverage against a waiting offensive unit.
coaching_points: Backcheck in direct routes to assigned defensive responsibilities.
First player back pressures the puck while the next layers protect net-front and slot areas.
Offensive players support the puck closely and attack the net.
Communicate continuously as roles change from offense to defense.

title: Drop Down 4 on 2
description: A full-ice 4-on-2 rush progression where forwards drop into varied support routes around a defenseman, organize into entry roles, and attack with interchangeable positions before the play reverses.
coaching_points: Vary low support, stretch, and middle routes through the neutral zone.
Fill wide, kick-out, and middle trailer roles with timing.
Defensemen maintain gap and protect the middle.
All players stay adaptable as positions interchange during the rush.

title: 5 Player - Every Pass a One Touch
description: Five players regroup through the neutral zone and attack up ice while every pass must be completed in one touch, forcing scanning, timing, communication, and continuous movement.
coaching_points: Know the next passing option before receiving the puck.
Keep sticks on the ice and communicate constantly.
All five players continue moving through the regroup and attack.
End the rep if a player needs more than one touch to reinforce speed of decision.

title: 4 v 3 Pass Between 2 Players
description: An in-zone 4-on-3 game where the offensive team must complete a pass between two defenders to a moving teammate before it is allowed to shoot.
coaching_points: Offensive players keep moving to open seams between defenders.
Time cuts through the defense with the puck carrier's readiness.
Defenders keep sticks in lanes and angle attackers away from the middle.
Reward both successful seam passes and goals.

title: The Ottawa Drill
description: A two-stage drill that begins with a down-low 3-on-2 and then, on the whistle, turns into a full-ice 5-on-5 as both groups join a second 3-on-2 moving the opposite direction.
coaching_points: Create 2-on-1 situations inside the initial 3-on-2.
Players without the puck jump to open ice and support closely.
Communicate through the transition into the full-ice phase.
Defenders regain structure quickly as the play expands to 5-on-5.

title: Offensive Advantage 3 vs 3
description: A 3-on-3 small-area game split into offensive and defensive halves. All three attackers may enter the offensive half, but only two defenders may enter their defensive half, creating a 3-on-2 advantage.
coaching_points: Players recognize how many teammates are in each half and adjust immediately.
Offense uses the numerical advantage before the defense can recover.
Players anticipate turnovers so they are not exposed in transition.
Communicate constantly to manage the half-ice restrictions.
